name: Bug Report
about: Report a bug or unexpected behavior in the Thunders Robotics project
title: '[BUG] '
labels: bug, triage
assignees: ''
---

## 🐛 Bug Description
A clear and concise description of what the bug is. 
*(e.g., The motor on the left drivetrain stops responding after 5 minutes of operation.)*

## 🔄 Steps to Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Power on the robot / Run the code with '...'
2. Trigger the specific mechanism / Click on '....'
3. Move the joystick to position '....'
4. See error / Observe the unexpected behavior

## ✅ Expected Behavior
A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen.
*(e.g., The left drivetrain motor should run smoothly without stopping until the command is halted.)*

## ❌ Actual Behavior
A clear and concise description of what actually happened.
*(e.g., The motor stalls, produces a buzzing sound, and the robot drifts to the right.)*

## 🤖 Environment & Hardware Context
Please complete the following information about the setup where the bug occurred:

- **Robot Name/ID:** [e.g., Competition Bot v2 / Practice Chassis]
- **Hardware Component:** [e.g., Drivetrain / Shooter / Intake / Arm]
- **Controller/Brain:** [e.g., VEX V5 Brain / roboRIO / Raspberry Pi 4]
- **Motor/Sensor IDs:** [e.g., Port 1-4 (Drivetrain Left) / Pigeon IMU]
- **Software/Firmware Version:** [e.g., WPILib 2024.1.1 / VEXos 1.0.13 / ROS2 Humble]
- **Operating System:** [e.g., Windows 11 / Ubuntu 22.04]

## 📸 Screenshots & Videos
If applicable, add screenshots or videos to help explain your problem. 
*(A video of the robot behaving unexpectedly is highly recommended for hardware/physics-related bugs).*

## 📋 Error Logs / Stack Trace
If there are any error messages printed to the console, driver station, or terminal, paste them here. 
*Please use code blocks (```) for readability.*

```text
Paste your error logs here...
```

## 💡 Possible Solution (Optional)
If you have an idea of what might be causing the bug or how to fix it, describe it here. 
*(e.g., Might be a CAN bus timeout issue, or PID gains are too high causing oscillation.)*

## 📌 Additional Context
Add any other context about the problem here. 
*(e.g., This only happens when the battery voltage drops below 11V, or it worked fine before the last code commit.)*
```
